intended_object: The n-th symmetric power Symⁿ_R(M) of an R-module M over a commutative ring R, viewed as an object of ModuleCat R. This is the degree-n part of the symmetric algebra, equivalently the quotient of M^{⊗n} by the permutation action. Inferred from the docstring, the module doc and the name.
explanation:
The body is `ModuleCat.of R (homogeneousSubmodule R M n)`, where `homogeneousSubmodule R M n` is defined as `(LinearMap.range (SymmetricAlgebra.ι R M)) ^ n`. That is the R-span of all products of n generators ι(m₁)⋯ι(mₙ) in Sym_R(M), which is exactly the degree-n graded piece Symⁿ(M) of the symmetric algebra. The library supports this identification: the pieces form the grading of the symmetric algebra, the degree-0 piece is identified with R and the degree-1 piece with M, and it is compatible with base change and with the MvPolynomial comparison when M has a basis.

The construction does not depend on any choice. It is functorial and is the standard symmetric power over a commutative ring.

On generality: the symmetric algebra needs a commutative (semi)ring, and `ModuleCat R` needs a ring, so `CommRing R` is the natural setting. Mathlib's `SymmetricPower R (Fin n) M` (notation `Sym[R]^n M`) defines the same object as a quotient of the tensor power. However, it needs the index type to live in R's universe, which is why the module docstring chooses the homogeneous-piece model. Mathlib has no `ModuleCat` version of symmetric powers; this definition is the analogue of `ModuleCat.exteriorPower`. So it is not too narrow, and it is faithful.
